$comment: Allowlist for scripts/check-scan-findings.mjs, the gate over the scanners that run
outside the JS test suite: Trivy image and IaC scans, and the ZAP baseline, in
.github/workflows/security-scanning.yml.
The grammar is the same as scripts/semgrep-allowlist.json on purpose. A finding at
or above the job's severity floor with no entry fails CI. An entry past its expiry
fails CI even though the finding still matches, so an acceptance cannot outlive the
triage that justified it. An entry that matches nothing fails CI as stale.
"scanner" is "trivy" or "zap" and scopes the entry to one report, so a ZAP alert
can never excuse a Trivy CVE that happens to share its number. Omit "locations"
to accept a finding wherever it appears. For Trivy each value is matched as a
substring of the finding's location, which is "<target>:<package>@<version>" for a
vulnerability and the scanned path for a misconfiguration.
A ZAP alert becomes one finding per instance it lists, and every one of them has to
match. Its "id" is the alert reference, such as 10055-4, not the plugin id: plugin
10055 alone raises a dozen different Content-Security-Policy alerts, and accepting one
must not accept the rest. Each ZAP "locations" value is an absolute URL with no query
or fragment. It covers a URL on the same origin whose path is its path or continues it
past a "/", whatever the query, so /api-docs covers /api-docs/streaming but not
/api-docs-internal. ZAP lists only five URLs for an alert it marks systemic, so an
entry scoped by "locations" vouches for the URLs the report shows and no others.
One alert reference can still cover more than its reason reviewed, so a ZAP entry can
pin what each instance reports. "otherinfo" has to equal a whole line of the
instance's other info: 10055-4 is raised for any directive that admits every host,
and that line lists which. "evidence" lists substrings, and the instance's evidence
has to contain one of them: for 90003 the evidence is the tag that lacks integrity.
Any other key in an entry fails CI, so a misspelled "locations", "otherinfo" or
"evidence" cannot leave the entry accepting every instance of its id.

entries.reason: Re-triaged 2026-10-23: img-src keeps https: because the page still renders images from hosts nobody can list in advance, and "otherinfo" limits this entry to that one directive. Those hosts are the favicon URLs a search provider returns with each result (WebSearchCard.tsx and CitationPill.tsx in packages/ui/unified-chat, ResearchPanel.tsx and WorkSessionPanel.tsx in apps/web), the iconUrl each connector registry entry carries (DirectoryGrid.tsx and ConnectorDetailView.tsx in packages/ui/ui/src/directory), and a reply image the reader chooses to load. MarkdownImage (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx) fetches unasked only same-origin, data:, blob: and the turn's own result and citation URLs; any other host stays a placeholder until the reader clicks, and then loads with no referrer. Map tiles and place photos no longer need it: they come through the same-origin /api/maps/tile and /api/maps/place-photo routes. Clearing the alert needs an authenticated, SSRF-hardened image proxy for those remaining URLs. That is a new server feature, not a header change, so this entry is renewed until that work is scheduled.

Re-triaged 2026-10-23: style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' because a nonce covers style elements, not style attributes. apps/web and packages/ui render 2,344 React style props across 217 non-test components, and Clerk's CSP guide, read 2026-10-23 at clerk.com/docs/guides/secure/best-practices/csp-headers, still says style-src 'unsafe-inline' is required for its components to inject their styles; removing that requirement is on Clerk's roadmap. Moving 'unsafe-inline' into style-src-attr and putting nonces on style elements would also need every runtime style injector (Clerk, Stripe, Leaflet) to carry the nonce, so it waits on that vendor change. script-src stays nonce-only, which scripts/check-security-response-headers.mjs enforces. The exemption is disclosed on /security and pinned by apps/web/app/trust/posture-claims.test.ts.

Re-triaged 2026-10-23: both flagged tags are emitted by @clerk/nextjs 7.9.9 itself (dist/esm/utils/clerk-script-tags.js): a script for /npm/@clerk/clerk-js@6/dist/clerk.browser.js and a preload for /npm/@clerk/ui@1/dist/ui.browser.js, both on the Frontend API host. The component builds them without an integrity attribute and has no prop to add one. Each URL names a major version that Clerk updates in place, so no pinned hash could match. The only way to change the URLs is the __internal_clerkJSUrl and __internal_clerkUIUrl props, which are internal and unsupported, so self-hosting a hashed copy is not a supported fix. "evidence" limits the entry to those two paths on clerk-ci.invalid, the host the scan's placeholder publishable key decodes to, so any other cross-origin script or preload without integrity still fails.

Public code samples, not server source. /api-docs renders the SDK examples in apps/web/content/api-docs/code-samples.json (the evidence is their 'for chunk in stream:'), and /gallery/<id> renders the fixed examples in apps/web/app/gallery/inspiration.ts (python-data-pipeline, sql-user-accounts-schema). Both pages exist to show code. Scoped to those two paths, so the same alert on any other URL still fails.

The sign-in and sign-up pages render the same form (apps/web/features/auth/AuthFlow.tsx), which declares method="post" only so that a submission no script handled can never write the password into the address bar (apps/web/features/auth/AuthEmailStep.tsx). Neither route has a POST handler: every credential goes from the browser to the identity provider through its own SDK, which carries its own request protection, so there is no state-changing request to this origin for a forged form to trigger. Scoped to /login and /signup, so the same alert on any other form still fails.
